hints: Work done links a force to the displacement produced in the direction of that force.
walkthrough: Identify the two quantities involved: force and displacement.
Only the displacement in the direction of the force contributes.
Therefore, work done is force multiplied by displacement in the direction of the force.

ai_rubric.observable: States that work done is force multiplied by displacement in the direction of the force.

hints: Describe both what is stored and what physical change causes it to be stored.
walkthrough: Elastic potential energy is stored energy.
It is stored when an object is stretched, compressed or otherwise elastically deformed.
Therefore, elastic potential energy is energy stored because of elastic deformation or a change of shape.

ai_rubric.observable: States that elastic potential energy is energy stored because an object is extended, compressed or changed in shape.

hints: Use the kinetic-energy formula with m = 0.40 kg and v = 0.30 m s⁻¹; remember to square the speed.
walkthrough: Use Eₖ = ½mv².
Substitute m = 0.40 kg and v = 0.30 m s⁻¹: Eₖ = ½ × 0.40 × 0.30².
Square the speed: 0.30² = 0.090.
Calculate ½ × 0.40 = 0.20.
In scientific notation, the initial kinetic energy is 1.8 × 10⁻² J.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes 0.40 kg and 0.30 m s⁻¹ to obtain 1.8 × 10⁻² J.

hints: The block’s kinetic energy is transferred to elastic potential energy in the spring.
On the graph of compression x against force F, the work done is still the area under a force–compression graph: ½Fₘₐₓxₘₐₓ.
walkthrough: When the block stops, its initial kinetic energy has been transferred to elastic potential energy in the spring.
From part (b)(i), the transferred energy is 1.8 × 10⁻² J.
The force rises linearly from zero to Fₘₐₓ while the compression rises to 8.0 cm, so the area representing work is triangular.
Convert the compression: 8.0 cm = 8.0 ÷ 100 = 0.080 m.
Set energy transferred equal to triangular area: 1.8 × 10⁻² = ½ × Fₘₐₓ × 0.080.
Calculate ½ × 0.080 = 0.040, giving 0.018 = 0.040Fₘₐₓ.
Rearrange: Fₘₐₓ = 0.018 ÷ 0.040 = 0.45 N.
The maximum force exerted on the spring is 0.45 N.

ai_rubric.observable: Equates the loss of kinetic energy to the work done on the spring or gain in elastic potential energy.
Uses the triangular graph area ½ × Fₘₐₓ × 0.080 m and equates it to 1.8 × 10⁻² J.

hints: The maximum force is 0.45 N; use F = ma with the 0.40 kg block.
walkthrough: Use Newton’s second law F = ma.
Rearrange for acceleration: a = F/m.
Substitute F = 0.45 N and m = 0.40 kg: a = 0.45 ÷ 0.40.
Calculate a = 1.125 m s⁻².
To two significant figures, the maximum deceleration is 1.1 m s⁻².

ai_rubric.observable: Uses 0.45 N and 0.40 kg to obtain a maximum deceleration of 1.1 m s⁻².

hints: Equilibrium depends on resultant force and acceleration, not simply on whether the object is moving or instantaneously at rest.
walkthrough: Before reaching the spring, the block moves at constant velocity.
Constant velocity means zero acceleration, so the resultant force is zero; the block is in equilibrium before it hits the spring.
At maximum compression, the speed is momentarily zero, but the spring exerts its maximum force on the block.
The resultant force and acceleration are therefore not zero at that instant; the block is not in equilibrium when its speed becomes zero.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the block is initially in equilibrium because constant velocity means zero resultant force.
States that the block is not in equilibrium at maximum compression because it is decelerating or has a non-zero resultant force.

hints: Equate the initial kinetic energy to the maximum elastic potential energy while the speed and spring constant remain fixed.
The resulting relationship has x₀ proportional to the square root of m.
walkthrough: At maximum compression, the initial kinetic energy is stored as elastic potential energy: ½mv² = ½kx₀².
Cancel the common factor ½ to obtain mv² = kx₀².
Rearrange: x₀² = (v²/k)m.
Because v and k remain constant, x₀² is proportional to m, so x₀ is proportional to √m.
The graph must start at the origin because m = 0 gives x₀ = 0.
A square-root graph rises as m increases but its gradient decreases, so draw a curve from the origin that becomes progressively less steep.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws a curved line beginning at the origin.
Draws the curve with a decreasing gradient as mass increases.
